evals.prompt: Can you audit the homepage of my plumbing business? https://example-plumbing.test. The business context is in .agents/business-context.md. Most visitors come from Google organic and Google Business Profile. We get calls, but hardly anyone uses the contact form.
evals.expected_output: Should capture the page and score the 5-second test blind, then read .agents/business-context.md and ask only for what it lacks. Should identify page type (homepage), one conversion goal (call or booked visit) and cold/local organic traffic. Should capture desktop 1440 px and mobile 390 px screenshots with agent-browser if available, or say which checks it could not verify. Should open with a 5-second test verdict scored 0-2 on what, why it matters, next step, why you and image. Should walk the checklist in order (message, structure, proof, CTA, friction, tech). Each finding should carry an A-* check ID or rule ID, a severity, quoted evidence or a screenshot region, and a concrete fix. Should group findings as Quick wins, High-impact changes and Test ideas, include What's working, and give 2-3 headline and CTA alternatives with rule-cited rationale. Should look at the post-click path (click-to-call for urgent jobs, short quote form) without submitting the live form. Should not forecast conversion lifts, and should offer to hand the rewrite to page-copy.
assertions: Scores the 5-second test before reading the business context, then reads .agents/business-context.md before asking questions
Identifies page type, conversion goal and traffic temperature
Captures or requests desktop and mobile views, or marks visual checks as not verified
Opens with a 5-second test verdict and a score out of 10
Every finding cites a check ID or rule ID (e.g. A-C2, HERO-02, CTA-02)
Every finding includes evidence (quoted copy, selector or screenshot region) and a concrete fix
Output has Quick wins, High-impact changes and Test ideas sections
Output has a What's working section
Provides 2-3 headline or CTA alternatives with rationale
Does not submit the live contact form without permission
Does not promise a specific conversion lift or quote reference stats as fact
Offers to hand the rewrite to page-copy

evals.prompt: We run Google Ads for our physiotherapy clinic and send the clicks to /back-pain. About 900 visitors a month, 1.1% book an appointment. Our marketing guy wants to add a '10,000 happy patients' counter and an 'Only 2 spots left this week!' banner to create urgency. We see around 40 new patients a month and usually have open slots. What should we fix on that page?
evals.expected_output: Should note that no business context file exists and run a short inline mini-brief (ideal customer, one job and primary CTA, pricing stance, proof available, locale) or draft from the page and mark items inferred. Should treat this as a paid landing page: ask for the ad and judge message match (STRUCT-03, A-M10) and whether the page has nav or links out. Should flag the proposed patient counter and fake scarcity banner as Critical trust/legal risks (PROOF-13, SCAR-01) and refuse to recommend them; may suggest a truthful capacity line only if capacity is really limited. Should recommend collecting real proof and use placeholders such as [PROOF NEEDED: ...] instead of inventing testimonials or numbers. Should explain that ~900 visitors a month is too little for most A/B tests (MEAS-01) and recommend before/after comparison, with any test ideas written as hypotheses. Output should follow the contract: 5-second verdict, Quick wins, High-impact changes, Test ideas, What's working.
assertions: Notices the missing business context file and runs a mini-brief or marks inferred context
Treats the page as a paid landing page and checks message match with the ad
Asks for or references the ad copy
Flags the invented patient counter as fake or unverifiable proof (PROOF-13 or A-P6)
Flags the 'Only 2 spots left' banner as fake scarcity (SCAR-01) and does not recommend it
Uses [PROOF NEEDED: ...] placeholders instead of inventing testimonials or numbers
States that traffic is too low for most A/B tests and recommends before/after measurement (MEAS-01)
Test ideas use a hypothesis format
Output starts with a 5-second test verdict
Output has Quick wins, High-impact changes, Test ideas and What's working sections

evals.prompt:
Audit the homepage of our Belgian web agency. The site is Dutch-first. Hero HTML:
Home | Over ons | Diensten | Cases | Blog | Jobs | Contact | Klantenlogin

Welkom bij Pixelwerk

Wij zijn een full-service digitaal bureau met passie voor innovatieve oplossingen op maat.

Meer infoContacteer ons. The footer only has our address and an Instagram icon. There are no testimonials on the site yet. Write the audit in English.
evals.expected_output: Should detect the BE locale and apply the BE/EU checks from be-eu.md: legal info (company name, legal form, KBO/BCE and VAT number), privacy notice at forms, cookie banner with an equal reject option, review rules, and Belgian Dutch language quality. Should mark legal items that be-eu.md flags as verify, not state them as settled law. Should quote the Dutch copy verbatim as evidence while writing findings in English. Should fail the 5-second test: 'Welkom bij' headline, jargon and cliché subhead ('full-service', 'innovatieve oplossingen op maat'), two vague buttons (HERO-01, HERO-02, COPY-01, COPY-02, CTA-02, CTA-03). Should flag the bloated nav with client login (STRUCT-05) and the social icon. Should give headline and CTA alternatives in Dutch, using only facts that are given, and use [PROOF NEEDED: ...] placeholders for missing testimonials rather than inventing any. Should note that visual checks (image, contrast, fold) could not be verified from HTML alone. May suggest belgisch-nederlands-redacteur for NL-BE copy if available.
assertions: Applies BE/EU checks (legal info with KBO/BCE or VAT number, cookie consent, privacy notice)
Marks uncertain legal items as verify rather than asserting them
Quotes Dutch copy verbatim as evidence and writes findings in English
Fails the 5-second test and flags the 'Welkom bij' headline (HERO-02 or COPY-02)
Flags vague CTAs 'Meer info' / 'Contacteer ons' with a CTA rule ID
Flags nav bloat and the client login link (STRUCT-05 or A-S3)
Provides Dutch headline and CTA alternatives without invented facts
Uses [PROOF NEEDED: ...] placeholders for missing testimonials
Marks visual checks as not verified because only HTML was provided
Includes a BE/EU checks section in the output

evals.prompt:
I'm a solo B2B operations consultant. Almost all my leads come from referrals and my LinkedIn posts, and lately a few said ChatGPT recommended me. Here's the text of my homepage (pasted below). Is it doing its job? About 300 visits a month.

Helping companies unlock operational excellence.
I partner with forward-thinking leaders to drive sustainable transformation.
[Get in touch]
Services: Process optimisation, Change management, Interim COO
About me: 20 years of experience across industries.
Contact: fill in the form (name, company, email, phone, budget, timeline, how can I help) and I'll get back to you.
evals.expected_output: Should treat the traffic as warm (referrals, LinkedIn, AI assistant) and judge accordingly: a shorter page is acceptable, but booking must be fast and visible (AI-04, contradiction C18). Should fail or heavily mark down the 5-second test for vague, jargon-heavy copy with no who/what/outcome (HERO-01, COPY-01, COPY-11) and missing differentiation (why you). Should flag the 7-field first-contact form and 'Get in touch' CTA, recommending a scheduler or a 3-4 field form (A-F1, A-F2, FORM-01, CTA-02). Should include an AI-search readiness section: logistics answers such as price, process and timeline (AI-01), niche signals and case studies (AI-02), consistent business facts (AI-03), and a 'How did you find us?' field with an AI assistant option (AI-06). Should note that only text was provided, so layout, imagery and mobile checks are not verified. Should say 300 visits/month cannot support A/B tests and recommend before/after measurement. Should not invent client names, results or testimonials, and should offer page-copy for the rewrite.
assertions: Classifies the traffic as warm and adjusts expectations (shorter page acceptable, fast booking path)
Flags jargon and vague value proposition with rule IDs (e.g. HERO-01, COPY-01)
Flags missing differentiation or 'why you'
Flags the long contact form and recommends a scheduler or 3-4 fields (A-F1, A-F2 or FORM-01)
Includes an AI-search readiness section citing AI-* rules
Recommends a 'How did you find us?' field that includes AI assistants (AI-06 or MEAS-02)
Marks layout, imagery and mobile checks as not verified
Recommends before/after measurement instead of A/B tests at this traffic level
Does not invent client names, results or testimonials
Offers to hand the rewrite to page-copy

evals.prompt: Audit our service page https://example-renovations.test/bathroom-renovation. It ranks on Google for 'bathroom renovation Ghent', and we also send our Google Ads there: the ad groups 'bathroom renovation', 'walk-in shower' and 'small bathroom ideas' all point to this page, although we have a separate walk-in shower page. We spend about EUR 1,500 a month on ads. The ad headline is 'Your new bathroom in 3 weeks, fixed price'. I'm travelling this week, so don't wait for my answers.
evals.expected_output: Should classify the traffic as paid + organic (a hybrid service page), not force one temperature. Should score the 5-second test blind before reading any context, with desktop and mobile scores, and grade A-M1 by the hero.md rule (<= 4/10 Critical, 5-6 High, >= 7 pass). Should judge the hero's message match against the ad headline (A-M10), keep the nav because the page also serves organic visitors but flag a nav button that competes with the hero CTA (C2 hybrid rule), and recommend a dedicated paid landing page given meaningful spend (STRUCT-03). Should flag that the 'walk-in shower' ad group lands on the generic page while a dedicated page exists (A-M11). Should capture with a named agent-browser session, fold shots with the cookie banner, and treat local lab vitals as lab only. Because the owner is unavailable, should proceed on inferred context and end with Questions for the owner (max 8). Copy alternatives in the page's language, findings in the user's language; no invented proof or lift forecasts.
assertions: Classifies traffic as paid + organic (hybrid) rather than a single temperature
Scores the 5-second test blind, per desktop and mobile, before reading business context
Grades A-M1 severity by score (<= 4 Critical, 5-6 High, >= 7 pass)
Checks hero message match against the ad headline (A-M10)
Keeps the nav for organic visitors but flags a competing nav CTA (C2)
Recommends a dedicated paid landing page given the ad spend (STRUCT-03)
Flags the walk-in shower ad group landing on the generic page (A-M11)
Uses a named agent-browser session and captures the fold with the cookie banner, or marks visual checks not verified
Proceeds without blocking and ends with a Questions for the owner section of at most 8 items
Does not invent proof or promise a conversion lift
